# Kinematics and Spins of Ultracool Dwarfs: Toward Substellar Galactic Archaeology and Gyrochronology

# Understanding substellar spin evolution and kinematics

## Low-mass brown dwarfs (<40 MJup) retain higher angular momentum

## Discovery of the first brown dwarf associated with Gaia Enceladus?

• Over the last few years, we developed the package SMART

(Hsu et al. 2021)1,9 to measure robust RV and vsini for UCDs with 10+ spectrometers including Keck/NIRSPEC1,2, SDSS/APOGEE3, and Gemini/IGRINS (Figure 1). • Our survey highlights with the BDKP Team include (1) first

kinematic evidence of stellar/substellar boundary at L4—L6 subtype1, (2) first RV verified T dwarf binaries1 and shortest period UCD binary2 and dozens of RV variable candidates3, and (3) radius inflation up to 25% was identified in 26 out of 41 isolated young brown dwarfs (0.05–0.1 MSun)3.

• It is widely known UCDs do not lose significant angular momentum compared to higher mass stars1,7, while it remains

unclear whether lower-mass UCDs sustain higher angular momenta after their disks dissipate (~10 Myr). • Along with our KPIC spin survey (see my Monday splinter talk), we also built a literature spin sample1,3,4,5,6,7 that has

221 objects with masses <100 MJup and well-determined ages, which is the largest known to date at this mass range. • Brown dwarfs between 5–40 MJup retain much higher angular momenta compared to low-mass stars and brown

dwarfs between 40–100 MJup after 10 Myr, when their initial angular momenta were set (Figure 2; Hsu et al. 2026).

• We conduct the first JWST NIRSpec metal-poor brown dwarf

kinematic survey with JWST Arcana Team (GO-4668; PI Burgasser). • We employ a fitting method to fit JWST/NIRSpec G395H spectra

(R~3,000) and show that our G395H RVs can achieve a systematic uncertainty of 5 km/s (vs objects with high-resolution RVs). • Our kinematic analysis indicate the possible first brown dwarf

associated with Gaia Enceladus merger remnant (Meisner, Burgasser, Hsu et al. submitted), and another brown dwarf associated with the Thamnos stream (Figure 3; Hsu et al. in prep).
